strategy.summary: CART-12 prices the cart at checkout through cartTotal(items, { coupon }) in src/cart.js: a 10% bulk discount at 10+ items in total, the SAVE5 coupon after the bulk discount with goods floored at $0, refusal of any other coupon, and shipping of $4.99 unless the discounted goods reach $50 (an empty cart is free). Unit tests in Vitest call cartTotal with literal carts and check the exact total. Reading the code shows a likely defect: bulkDiscount uses `itemCount > BULK_THRESHOLD`, so a cart of exactly 10 items gets no discount.
inScope: cartTotal pricing: bulk discount, SAVE5 coupon, coupon refusal, shipping and empty cart
outOfScope: UI or API for checkout: the repo only has the pricing module
assumptions: Coupon codes match exactly and are case-sensitive, so 'save5' is another code and is refused (the code uses Object.hasOwn on { SAVE5 })
Refusal is a thrown Error; the tests check it is an Error whose message names the submitted code, because the module exports no error code
'Goods' means subtotal less bulk discount less coupon, floored at 0, which is what the shipping threshold applies to
openQuestions: bulkDiscount uses `> BULK_THRESHOLD` (10), so exactly 10 items gets no discount, against AC1's '10 or more'. TC1 is kept as an expected failure and reported as a defect.

Shipping is free when the goods cost $50 or more after discounts, otherwise $4.99

defects.title: Cart of exactly 10 items gets no bulk discount
defects.description: AC1: a cart with 10 or more items in total should get 10% off. bulkDiscount in src/cart.js uses `itemCount(items) > BULK_THRESHOLD`, so a cart of exactly 10 items is charged in full. The fix would be `>=`.
defects.evidence: cartTotal([{price:10,quantity:4},{price:10,quantity:6}]) returns 100, but 90 is expected. The it.fails test passes, which confirms the assertion fails.

review.standard: General: recognise the app's behaviour by its structure, not the wording of a message; when only a message tells refusals apart, check the part the test controls (the submitted code)
review.summary: The refusal test checks the whole message text `Unknown coupon: ${code}`. The accepted strategy and the standard ask only that the message name the submitted code.
review.failureScenario: Say cart.js rewords the error to `Coupon SAVE10 is not valid` but still throws an Error that names the code. All three it.each rows then fail even though the refusal works as AC3 requires. The '' row can't use a plain toContain(code), because toContain('') matches any message. So assert the instance plus a check that names the code, e.g. a regex ending in the code, and keep an exact check only for the empty code.
